intended_object: The simple right vertex module S_v of the signless preprojective algebra Π at a vertex v. It is the cokernel of the incoming-arrow map ⊕_{b : i → v} e_i Π → e_v Π, (z_b) ↦ ∑ b z_b, so it is e_v Π modulo its arrow ideal, which is one copy of k concentrated at v. This is inferred from the docstring, the module documentation and the Etingof–Eu vertex Koszul complex.
explanation:
Right Π-modules are encoded as left Πᵐᵒᵖ-modules, and e_v Π is taken as the principal left ideal generated by op(e_v) in Πᵐᵒᵖ. The definition is the quotient of this ideal by the range of `signlessPreprojectiveKoszulRight`. That map sends (z_b) to ∑ b·z_b in Π, with b running over the arrows into v. Its range is exactly the arrow part of e_v Π, so the quotient is the vertex module S_v.

The library confirms this. `signlessPreprojectiveVertexAugmentation_eq_zero_iff` shows that the quotient kills exactly the elements whose coefficient at v is zero. `signlessPreprojectiveVertexModuleEquiv` identifies the quotient with k as a k-module.

The setting is a finite quiver with an arrow reversal over a commutative ring k. This is the standard setting for preprojective algebras: the defining relation and the incoming-arrow sum need finitely many arrows. Mathlib has no preprojective algebra and no vertex simple module, so there is no more general Mathlib definition this one should have used. The definition matches its docstring and the intended object.
